cases.name: cp comparison: copies a file into an existing directory
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir d; echo A > a.md; cp a.md d; echo rc=$?; cat d/a.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: copies a file into an existing directory with a trailing slash
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir d; echo A > a.md; cp a.md d/; echo rc=$?; cat d/a.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r copies a directory into an existing directory
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s d; echo X > s/x.md; cp -r s d; echo rc=$?; cat d/s/x.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -R copies a directory into an existing directory
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s d; echo X > s/x.md; cp -R s d; echo rc=$?; cat d/s/x.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r copies a directory as the destination when it does not exist
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s; echo X > s/x.md; cp -r s newdir; echo rc=$?; cat newdir/x.md; ls newdir; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r with a trailing slash on the source
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s d; echo X > s/x.md; cp -r s/ d; echo rc=$?; cat d/s/x.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r with a trailing slash on the destination
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s d; echo X > s/x.md; cp -r s d/; echo rc=$?; cat d/s/x.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r merges into an existing destination subtree
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir -p s d/s; echo X > s/x.md; echo K > d/s/k.md; cp -r s d; echo rc=$?; cat d/s/k.md d/s/x.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r copies nested directories
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir -p s/n; echo X > s/n/x.md; echo Y > s/y.md; cp -r s d; echo rc=$?; cat d/n/x.md d/y.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: copies several files into a directory
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir d; echo A > a.md; echo B > b.md; cp a.md b.md d; echo rc=$?; cat d/a.md d/b.md; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: preserves the source file mode
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; echo A > a.md; chmod 755 a.md; cp a.md b.md; echo rc=$?; test -x b.md && echo exec; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: a directory source without -r is omitted
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s; echo X > s/x.md; cp s d; echo rc=$?; ls; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: missing destination operand
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; echo A > a.md; cp a.md; echo rc=$?; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: missing file operand
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; cp; echo rc=$?; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: nonexistent source
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; cp nope.md d.md; echo rc=$?; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: several operands need a directory target
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; echo A > a.md; echo B > b.md; echo C > c.md; cp a.md b.md c.md; echo rc=$?; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: several operands need an existing target
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; echo A > a.md; echo B > b.md; cp a.md b.md nodir; echo rc=$?; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r refuses to copy a directory into itself
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir -p a/b; echo C > a/b/c.md; cp -r a a/b; echo rc=$?; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: -r cannot overwrite a non-directory with a directory
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir s; echo X > s/x.md; echo F > f; cp -r s f; echo rc=$?; cat f; rm -rf $D

cases.name: cp comparison: a failing source does not stop the remaining copies
cases.script: D=/tmp/jb_cp_$$; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D; cd $D; mkdir d; echo A > a.md; cp nope.md a.md d; echo rc=$?; cat d/a.md; rm -rf $D
